nodes.summary: There exists a group $G$ of spread exactly $1$: for every nontrivial $x \in G$ there is $y \in G$ with $\langle x, y \rangle = G$, but for every natural number $m > 1$ there are nontrivial elements $x_1, \dots, x_m \in G$ such that no single $y \in G$ satisfies $\langle x_i, y \rangle = G$ for all $i$. This answers Kourovka Problem 21.38 affirmatively.
nodes.title: There is a group of spread exactly one

nodes.summary: The conjecture that there exists a group of spread exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Existence of a group of spread exactly one (Kourovka 21.38)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has spread at least $k$, for a natural number $k$, when for every family $x_1, \dots, x_k$ of nontrivial elements of $G$, not necessarily distinct, there is an element $y \in G$ such that the subgroup $\langle x_i, y \rangle$ generated by $x_i$ and $y$ is all of $G$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Spread at least $k$

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has spread exactly $k$, for a natural number $k$, when $G$ has spread at least $k$ and, for every natural number $m > k$, $G$ does not have spread at least $m$.
nodes.title: Spread exactly $k$

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. The spread $s(G)$ of $G$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of the natural numbers $k$ such that for any non-trivial elements $x_1, \dots, x_k$ of $G$ (not necessarily distinct) there exists $y \in G$ such that the subgroup $\langle x_i, y \rangle$ generated by $x_i$ and $y$ is all of $G$ for every $i$. In particular $s(G) = \infty$ when there is no largest such $k$.
nodes.title: Spread of a group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. Then the spread $s(G)$ is at least $2$ if and only if every proper quotient of $G$ is cyclic, that is, $G/N$ is cyclic for every non-trivial normal subgroup $N$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Burness–Guralnick–Harper spread theorem
